Car Loan Data Analysis and Imputation
```{r}
# Option 1: tidyverse (recommended)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)

# Adjust filename if needed (e.g., "00_car_loan_data.csv")
df <- read_csv("car_loan_data.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

cat("Data shape:", paste(dim(df), collapse = " x "), "\n\n")

cat("First few rows:\n")
print(head(df))

cat("\nData types and missing values:\n")
glimpse(df)

cat("\nMissing values per column:\n")
print(colSums(is.na(df)))

cols <- c("salary_range", "driver_tenure")

```



2. Missing Data Statistics
```{r}

# 1) Number of rows with missing values in any column
sum(!complete.cases(df[cols]))

# 2) Number of rows with missing values in both columns
sum(rowSums(is.na(df[cols])) == length(cols))

# 3) Number of rows with missing values only in salary_range
sum(is.na(df$salary_range) & !is.na(df$driver_tenure))

# 4) Number of rows with missing values only in driver_tenure
sum(!is.na(df$salary_range) & is.na(df$driver_tenure))

# 5) Total number of missing cells
sum(is.na(df[cols]))

table(df$salary_range, useNA="ifany")

```


3. Imputing Missing Values for Salary Range
```{r}
df <- read_csv("car_loan_data.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
library(randomForest)

# Target variable
target_col <- "salary_range"
exclude_cols <- c("repaid", "driver_tenure") # Columns to exclude

# Mark missing values
is_missing <- is.na(df[[target_col]])
train_df <- df[!is_missing, ]
predict_df <- df[is_missing, ]

# 1. Check training label distribution
cat("Distribution of salary_range in training set:\n")
print(table(train_df[[target_col]], useNA="ifany"))

# 2. Feature columns (excluding target and excluded columns)
feature_cols <- setdiff(names(df), c(target_col, exclude_cols))
X_train <- train_df[, feature_cols, drop=FALSE]
X_pred  <- if (nrow(predict_df) > 0) predict_df[, feature_cols, drop=FALSE] else NULL

# 3. Convert character to factor; ensure training set is factorized
for (nm in names(X_train)) {
  if (is.character(X_train[[nm]])) X_train[[nm]] <- as.factor(X_train[[nm]])
}
for (nm in names(X_pred)) {
  if (is.character(X_pred[[nm]])) X_pred[[nm]] <- as.factor(X_pred[[nm]])
}

# 4. Simple imputation for training features using training set statistics (mean for numeric, mode for categorical)
get_mode <- function(x) {
  ux <- unique(x[!is.na(x)])
  if (length(ux)==0) return(NA)
  ux[which.max(tabulate(match(x, ux)))]
}
numeric_cols <- names(X_train)[sapply(X_train, is.numeric)]
categorical_cols <- setdiff(names(X_train), numeric_cols)

for (col in numeric_cols) {
  if (any(is.na(X_train[[col]]))) {
    X_train[[col]][is.na(X_train[[col]])] <- mean(X_train[[col]], na.rm=TRUE)
  }
}
for (col in categorical_cols) {
  if (any(is.na(X_train[[col]]))) {
    X_train[[col]][is.na(X_train[[col]])] <- get_mode(X_train[[col]])
  }
  X_train[[col]] <- as.factor(X_train[[col]])
}

# 5. Ensure prediction set factor levels match training set
if (!is.null(X_pred)) {
  for (col in categorical_cols) {
    if (col %in% names(X_pred)) {
      # Convert prediction set values to training set levels; unknown values become NA
      X_pred[[col]] <- factor(as.character(X_pred[[col]]), levels = levels(X_train[[col]]))
      # If there are NAs (due to levels in prediction set not in training set), impute with training set mode
      if (any(is.na(X_pred[[col]]))) {
        X_pred[[col]][is.na(X_pred[[col]])] <- get_mode(X_train[[col]])
      }
    } else {
      stop("Prediction set missing categorical column from training set: ", col)
    }
  }
  for (col in numeric_cols) {
    if (col %in% names(X_pred) && any(is.na(X_pred[[col]]))) {
      X_pred[[col]][is.na(X_pred[[col]])] <- mean(X_train[[col]], na.rm=TRUE)
    }
  }
}

# 6. Check if training labels are extremely imbalanced
tbl_y <- table(train_df[[target_col]])
print(tbl_y)
# If a class is too small, consider using sampsize or classwt. Here we train first without setting these.

# 7. Train random forest (consider sampsize for balancing)
set.seed(123)
rf_model <- randomForest(
  x = X_train,
  y = as.factor(train_df[[target_col]]),
  ntree = 300,
  importance = TRUE
)

print(rf_model)        # Check OOB error / confusion
print(importance(rf_model))

# 8. Predict and check distribution
if (!is.null(X_pred) && nrow(X_pred) > 0) {
  y_pred <- predict(rf_model, X_pred)
  cat("Prediction distribution:\n"); print(table(y_pred))
  # Fill back into original dataframe
  df[[target_col]][is_missing] <- as.character(y_pred)
} else {
  cat("No prediction needed (no missing values)\n")
}

# 9. If predictions are still almost all one class, try using sampsize for balanced training:
# For example, if training set has two classes A/B, you can set sampsize = c(nA, nA) (using smaller class count)
# sampsize <- rep(min(tbl_y), length(tbl_y))  # Generate by number of classes
# rf_model_bal <- randomForest(x = X_train, y = as.factor(train_df[[target_col]]),
#                             ntree = 300, sampsize = sampsize, importance=TRUE)
# y_pred2 <- predict(rf_model_bal, X_pred)
# table(y_pred2)

# 10. Finally save the results
write.csv(df, "car_loan_data_salary_imputed.csv", row.names = FALSE)
cat("Saved car_loan_data_salary_imputed.csv\n")
df <- read_csv("car_loan_data_salary_imputed.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
table(df$salary_range, useNA="ifany")

```


4. Accuracy Assessment for Salary Range Prediction
```{r}
# If comparing true labels vs predicted labels
# Re-predict on training set to get training set predictions

y_pred_train <- predict(rf_model, X_train)

# Calculate accuracy
accuracy <- mean(y_pred_train == train_df$salary_range)
cat(sprintf("Training set prediction accuracy: %.2f%%\n", accuracy * 100))

# View confusion matrix
library(caret)
confusionMatrix(
  data = as.factor(y_pred_train),
  reference = as.factor(train_df$salary_range)
)

```

5. Imputing Missing Values for Driver Tenure
```{r}
# ==============================
# Use random forest to predict / impute driver_tenure
# ==============================

library(randomForest)
library(dplyr)
df <- read_csv("car_loan_data_salary_imputed.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# 1️⃣ Mark missing values
is_missing <- is.na(df$driver_tenure)

# 2️⃣ Training set and prediction set
train_df <- df[!is_missing, ]
predict_df <- df[is_missing, ]

if (nrow(train_df) == 0) {
  cat("driver_tenure is completely missing, cannot train model\n")
} else {
  # Target column
  y <- train_df$driver_tenure
  
  # Feature columns: exclude target and unwanted columns
  exclude_cols <- c("driver_tenure", "repaid_loan_on_prev_car")
  feature_cols <- setdiff(names(df), exclude_cols)
  
  X_train <- train_df[, feature_cols, drop = FALSE]
  X_pred  <- if (nrow(predict_df) > 0) predict_df[, feature_cols, drop = FALSE] else NULL
  
  # Numeric and categorical columns
  numeric_cols <- names(X_train)[sapply(X_train, is.numeric)]
  categorical_cols <- setdiff(names(X_train), numeric_cols)
  
  # Mode function
  get_mode <- function(x) {
    ux <- unique(x[!is.na(x)])
    if (length(ux) == 0) return(NA)
    ux[which.max(tabulate(match(x, ux)))]
  }
  
  # Simple missing value imputation for training features (mean / mode)
  X_train_imputed <- X_train
  for (col in numeric_cols) {
    if (any(is.na(X_train_imputed[[col]]))) {
      X_train_imputed[[col]][is.na(X_train_imputed[[col]])] <- mean(X_train[[col]], na.rm = TRUE)
    }
  }
  for (col in categorical_cols) {
    if (any(is.na(X_train_imputed[[col]]))) {
      mode_val <- get_mode(X_train[[col]])
      X_train_imputed[[col]][is.na(X_train_imputed[[col]])] <- mode_val
    }
    X_train_imputed[[col]] <- as.factor(X_train_imputed[[col]])
  }
  
  # Train random forest model
  rf_model_tenure <- randomForest(
    x = X_train_imputed,
    y = y,  # tenure is typically a continuous numeric value
    ntree = 300,
    importance = TRUE
  )
  
  print(rf_model_tenure)
  
  # If there are missing rows that need prediction
  if (!is.null(X_pred) && nrow(X_pred) > 0) {
    X_pred_imputed <- X_pred
    # Impute missing prediction features using training set statistics
    for (col in numeric_cols) {
      if (any(is.na(X_pred_imputed[[col]]))) {
        X_pred_imputed[[col]][is.na(X_pred_imputed[[col]])] <- mean(X_train[[col]], na.rm = TRUE)
      }
    }
    for (col in categorical_cols) {
      if (any(is.na(X_pred_imputed[[col]]))) {
        mode_val <- get_mode(X_train[[col]])
        X_pred_imputed[[col]][is.na(X_pred_imputed[[col]])] <- mode_val
      }
      X_pred_imputed[[col]] <- factor(as.character(X_pred_imputed[[col]]),
                                      levels = levels(X_train_imputed[[col]]))
    }
    
    # Predict missing tenure values
    y_pred <- predict(rf_model_tenure, X_pred_imputed)
    df$driver_tenure[is_missing] <- y_pred
    cat(sprintf("✅ Used random forest to predict and impute driver_tenure, total %d records.\n", length(y_pred)))
  } else {
    cat("driver_tenure has no missing values, no imputation needed.\n")
  }
}

# 3️⃣ Check results
summary(df$driver_tenure)
sum(is.na(df$driver_tenure))

# 4️⃣ Export results
write.csv(df, "car_loan_data_with_tenure.csv", row.names = FALSE)
cat("✅ Exported file with imputed driver_tenure: car_loan_data_with_tenure.csv\n")
df <- read_csv("car_loan_data_with_tenure.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
table(df$driver_tenure, useNA="ifany")

```


6. Performance Evaluation for Driver Tenure Prediction
```{r}
# Predict on training set
y_pred_train <- predict(rf_model_tenure, X_train_imputed)

# Actual values
y_true <- train_df$driver_tenure

# R² coefficient of determination
r2 <- cor(y_pred_train, y_true)^2

# RMSE root mean squared error
rmse <- sqrt(mean((y_pred_train - y_true)^2))

# MAE mean absolute error
mae <- mean(abs(y_pred_train - y_true))

cat(sprintf("Random forest prediction performance for driver_tenure:\n"))
cat(sprintf("R²  = %.3f\n", r2))
cat(sprintf("RMSE = %.3f\n", rmse))
cat(sprintf("MAE  = %.3f\n", mae))

```
